solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old Italian with very large buttocks

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
can is American slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A rude description of some ancient Roman with an enormous rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is marked on very large garments; CAN is US slang for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscans were an ancient people of southern Italy whose language was a relative of Latin.

clue.text: Firm approval after King dropped

indicators.note: in a down entry a letter that is dropped slides further down the column, landing inside the rest

parts.note: okay is a word of approval
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A company gets the nod once its king has been deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of OKAY is not lost but moved one place lower, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaky describes something hard and solid like oak timber, hence firm.

clue.text: Ghostly procession showing eager desire but failing to start

indicators.note: a word failing to start has lost its opening letter

parts.note: an aspiration is a keen ambition

explanation.surface: A phantom parade seems driven by longing that never gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ghostly' points to the Holy Ghost: this is a theological term, not a spooky one.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology spiration is the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son.

clue.text: Old-fashioned sounding instruments

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word that is said like another, not spelt like it

parts.note: corny means trite and dated

explanation.surface: Antique instruments that make a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Corni is the Italian plural of corno, the horn, as written in orchestral scores.

clue.text: Moderate administrative trainee's fit

parts.note: AT is the abbreviation for an administration trainee in the British civil service
a fit of rage is a temper

explanation.surface: A junior office worker throws a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To attemper is an old verb meaning to soften or regulate, which is to moderate.

clue.text: Leaders in part of string section missing gut

indicators.note: a gut is the middle of something, so missing it means the central letters drop out

parts.note: cellos sit in the string section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: Principal players in an orchestra's strings have lost their gut strings.
explanation.walkthrough: The two middle letters LL are removed from the six.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief executive officers are company bosses, so they are leaders.

clue.text: Politician's dry externally always

indicators.note: something placed externally sits on the outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: sere means withered and dry
an MP is a Member of Parliament; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A politician who is perpetually dull and dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Politician's dry externally' as the politician has dry on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sempre is the Italian musical direction meaning always, as in sempre forte.

clue.text: Does for clubs sharing meals

indicators.note: one item sharing the meals takes a place among them, sitting inside

parts.note: suppers are evening meals
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone cooks for a club that eats together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does for' sounds like a cleaner's job, but here it means to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck it, and to do for something is likewise to destroy it.

clue.text: Relaxed and satisfied having given up place

indicators.note: having given something up, the word no longer contains it

parts.note: pleased means content
PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: Someone content and at ease after retiring from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or made less tense, so slackened or relaxed.

clue.text: Long set on oily stuff used in medicines

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece set on another sits above it in the column

parts.note: to pine is to long for something
tar is thick oily black matter

explanation.surface: A yearning fixed upon an ointment's ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'oily stuff' do double duty: they give the second piece and also begin the full definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine tar, distilled from pine wood, has long been used in ointments and soaps for skin complaints.

clue.text: Trying person in lower tier heads off

indicators.note: with heads off each word loses its first letter and keeps the rest

parts.note: less means lower in amount
a layer is a tier

explanation.surface: A tiresome person seated in the lower tier of a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' suggests tiresome, but it means attempting.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to attempt, so an essayer is someone who tries.

clue.text: Old druggists accepted endless fuss associated with tooth decay

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: A marks a bill as accepted
pother is commotion or fuss
caries is the dental term for decay

explanation.surface: Old chemists put up with constant complaints about rotten teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Apothecaries were the historical dispensers of medicine, predecessors of pharmacists.

clue.text: Large number you once found on beach

parts.note: thou is the archaic word for you
the sands are a beach

explanation.surface: Someone you used to know was discovered on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large number' is a noun phrase, matching the plural of a thousand used for a great many.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands is the everyday hyperbole for a great many.

clue.text: Bob and Hal recalled reciprocal units

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated S in old British money
Hal is the familiar name of Prince Henry in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Two old friends called Bob and Hal are summoned back.
explanation.definitionFit: The yrneh is a unit of reciprocal inductance, the henry spelt backwards just as the mho is the reversed ohm.

clue.text: African's money lost in a sweep

definitions.note: possessive phrase; the answer is the coin itself

indicators.note: letters that are lost have wandered out of their order and must be put right

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An African gambler loses cash in a sweepstake.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweep here is a sweepstake, a lottery on a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The pesewa is the coin of Ghana, a hundredth of a cedi.

clue.text: Energy change accommodating English and Scottish poll (9, two words)

indicators.note: something accommodating gives others room inside it

parts.note: to waver is to fluctuate or vary
E is the abbreviation for English
pow is Scots for the head, and a poll is a head

explanation.surface: Political momentum shifts in an election held across England and Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' looks like a vote but is the old word for a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Wave power is energy generated from the motion of sea waves.

clue.text: Spirit shown by Welshman second to none initially

parts.note: Dai is the stock Welsh first name in crosswords
a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: initially points to just the opening letter of that word

parts.note: the opening letter of none

explanation.surface: A Welshman whose spirit is second to nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to none' reads as an idiom for unbeatable, but the words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A daimon, or daemon, is a guiding spirit in Greek thought.

clue.text: New dancing routine that comes without a charge

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: dancing letters jig about out of their written order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh dance routine offered free of any fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a charge' sounds like no fee, but means electrically neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is a subatomic particle that carries no electric charge.

clue.text: Part of muscle remarkably showing hardening of tissues

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a piece of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Some muscle is unusually stiff, a sign of tissue hardening.
explanation.definitionFit: Sclerema is a medical condition in which the skin and the tissue beneath it harden.

clue.text: Sounds like a smart person cracks awkward task amateur ignored

indicators.note: something that cracks a shell breaks into it and sits inside
awkward suggests something clumsily arranged, so the letters are jumbled
a word ignored is left out of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for amateur
a smart person is chic, stylish

explanation.surface: A clever person tackles a difficult job, with the amateur left out.
explanation.walkthrough: TASK without its A leaves three letters to jumble, and the stylish word goes between the first and the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchicks are the clicking sounds made with the tongue, as when urging on a horse.

clue.text: Ghanaian people from a ramshackle hut spoken of

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something spoken of is heard rather than read, so the sound counts

parts.note: a shanty is a crude hut

explanation.surface: Villagers emerge from a tumbledown shack.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashanti are an Akan people of central Ghana, once a powerful kingdom.

clue.text: Act as lookout in stronghold chamber underground

parts.note: the keep is the fortified tower of a castle
a cave is an underground hollow

explanation.surface: A sentry posted in a castle's subterranean room.
explanation.walkthrough: Cave (said KAY-vee) is Latin for 'beware!', old British public-school slang shouted as a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep cave is schoolboy slang for keeping watch so others are not caught.

clue.text: Chasing odd character seen around island railway

indicators.note: around puts the first word on the outside of what follows

parts.note: a cure is an eccentric person
Is is the abbreviation for island
the El is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A peculiar figure spotted wandering an island's railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' means engraving metal, not pursuit; a cure is old slang for an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciselure is the craft of chasing, decorating metal by chiselling and engraving.

clue.text: Regret endlessly boosted electrical unit

indicators.note: in a down entry, boosted means pushed upwards, so read from the bottom
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to repent is to regret

explanation.surface: Remorse that is endlessly amplified.
explanation.definitionFit: The neper is a logarithmic unit for ratios of field quantities, used in electrical engineering.

clue.text: Guide perhaps not party's leader abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters spread into a new order
not means this letter is to be left out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so take the word's first letter

parts.note: the first letter of party

explanation.surface: A tour guide abroad might be no party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like a definition-by-example marker, but it is the letters to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters.

clue.text: Opener for England gets outside of mark for wide

indicators.note: to get outside something is to surround it, wrapping it inside

parts.note: Jason Roy opened the batting for England's cricket team
o' is a clipped form of of, as in o'clock
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A cricket opener plays outside the off-stump mark for a wide.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide in cricket is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach; here wide simply means spacious.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means having plenty of space, so broad or wide.

clue.text: Rather silly how the Queen is represented

parts.note: in describes the manner: in a given form
the Queen is written as an ER, the royal cipher Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark on the foolishness of royal portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen is represented 'in an ER': ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaner is the comparative of inane, meaning more foolish or empty-headed.

clue.text: Exclusive about rector making harsh noise

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a scoop is an exclusive news story
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A newspaper exclusive about a vicar causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Scroop is a dialect word for a grating or scraping sound.

clue.text: Jack in house mostly, a lower one

indicators.note: in places this item inside the other word
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A card game in a house where one player is lowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lower one' refers back to 'house': the definition needs the parliamentary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sejm is the lower house of the Polish parliament.

clue.text: Do without missing van for dock

indicators.note: the van is the front of a procession, so the first letter is missing

parts.note: if you can spare something you can do without it

explanation.surface: Someone manages without the van they needed to get to the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' looks like a vehicle but means the leading part, as in vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail is to cut it short, and to pare is to trim away.

clue.text: Stick with combine for field in the Caribbean

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
to piece things together is to combine them

explanation.surface: A farmer brings a stick and a combine harvester to the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' suggests a harvester in a field; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane piece is a sugar-cane field on a Caribbean plantation.

clue.text: Amazement with heartless JFK shooting before ultimately utter distress in Dallas

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken out
shooting suggests letters flying about and landing in new positions

parts.note: taken as written
the initials JFK without their middle F

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of utter

explanation.surface: Shock at the Kennedy assassination in Dallas, ending in utter anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Dallas' flags an American usage; the Kennedy story is pure decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Katzenjammer, from German 'cats' wailing', is US slang for a hangover or a state of distress.

clue.text: Roman officer appearing before wives returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: or is an archaic word for before, as in 'or ever'
ribs is jocular slang for wives, from Eve made of Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier turns up ahead of the wives coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a positional link but supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A sbirro is an Italian police officer, so a Roman one fits.

clue.text: Will's faith on show

parts.note: fay is a Shakespearean word for faith, Will being Shakespeare
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's religion is put on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Fayre is a mock-archaic spelling of fair, an exhibition or show.
